title: Generic functions and inference

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Generic functions and inference

children.text: A type parameter links an input type to an output type. Most of the skill is letting inference do the work rather than annotating call sites.
What this lesson covers
Relate argument and return types with a type parameter
Let inference fill in type arguments at the call site
Recognise when a generic adds nothing over a union
This lesson sits in Generics, part of TypeScript for Application Developers. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Relate argument and return types with a type parameter
Let inference fill in type arguments at the call site
Recognise when a generic adds nothing over a union

title: Constraints and default type parameters

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Constraints and default type parameters

children.text: Constraints say what a type parameter must at least be. Combined with keyof, they give you property access that stays typed.
What this lesson covers
Constrain a parameter with extends
Use keyof to type property access generically
Give a type parameter a sensible default
This lesson sits in Generics, part of TypeScript for Application Developers. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Constrain a parameter with extends
Use keyof to type property access generically
Give a type parameter a sensible default

title: Generic components in React

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Generic components in React

children.text: A typed list component should tell you what its render callback receives. Generic props are how a reusable component stays specific at each use.
What this lesson covers
Type a component over the shape of its items
Keep render props and callbacks correctly typed
Forward refs without losing the generic parameter
This lesson sits in Generics, part of TypeScript for Application Developers. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Type a component over the shape of its items
Keep render props and callbacks correctly typed
Forward refs without losing the generic parameter
proTip: If a reusable component takes items and hands them back to a callback, it wants a type parameter.

title: Conditional types and infer

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Conditional types and infer

children.text: A conditional type branches on assignability, and infer pulls a type out of the branch it matched. This is how utility types are built.
What this lesson covers
Branch a type on an extends check
Extract inner types with infer
Understand distribution over union members
This lesson sits in Advanced Types, part of TypeScript for Application Developers. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Branch a type on an extends check
Extract inner types with infer
Understand distribution over union members

title: Mapped types and key remapping

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Mapped types and key remapping

children.text: Mapped types transform every property of a type at once, which is where Partial, Readonly, and their friends come from.

Add or strip optional and readonly modifiers

title: Template literal types

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Template literal types

children.text: String types can be composed and pattern-matched, which lets you type things like event names and route paths precisely.
What this lesson covers
Compose string types from other types
Constrain string shapes such as event or route names
Combine template literals with key remapping
This lesson sits in Advanced Types, part of TypeScript for Application Developers. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Compose string types from other types
Constrain string shapes such as event or route names
Combine template literals with key remapping
proTip: Template literal types are excellent for typed event names, and a trap when used to parse arbitrary strings.
